findings.claim: The User Storage SPI contract for recovery codes changes in a way providers can see, and the patch documents none of it: no docs, release notes, upgrade guide or Javadoc. Providers now receive plaintext codes as a JSON list via updateCredential, must return Keycloak's internal hashed model from getCredentials, and are read before local storage.
findings.evidence: mattpocock: all 8 files are Java and none is under docs/; CONTRIBUTING.md:29 and :79 and PR-CHECKLIST.md:9 require docs; plaintext codes at CredentialHelper.java:117-123; federated read first at RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.java:56-62. open-code-review: the asymmetric contract (plaintext in, hashed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel out) is documented nowhere and no Javadoc was added. superpowers: neither the Javadoc of createRecoveryCodesCredential nor CredentialInputUpdater documents the asymmetric contract. All reasoned.
findings.reason: Accepted. Add provider-facing docs and Javadoc plus a release-note or upgrade-guide entry. Red check: on the pinned code, no doc or Javadoc describes the recovery-codes user-storage contract.

findings.claim: The fixture's isValid never consumes a code after a successful match, and the new test performs only one login, so single use is not exercised on the federated path.
findings.evidence: open-code-review: generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse())) with no state change afterwards (:325-340). superpowers: the fixture never consumes codes and the test (:241-262) does exactly one login. mattpocock: the test provider accepts any stored code every time (:326-341), and testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin checks a single login. ponytail: the fixture never marks codes as used.
findings.reason: Accepted test gap. Make the fixture remove a used code, and add a second login with the same code that must be rejected.

findings.claim: For federated recovery codes, core never enforces single use or tells user storage that a code was used. Consumption is left entirely to the provider's isValid.
findings.evidence: mattpocock: the local isValid (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.java:99-117) removes the used code via updateStoredCredential, but nothing on the federated path does, so codes held in user storage look reusable. open-code-review: consuming used codes is left entirely to the provider's isValid, and core never enforces single use for federated codes. superpowers: core delegates single-use enforcement to the storage provider, and nothing in the change says so. All reasoned.
findings.reason: ponytail: closing this needs an SPI design decision (core cannot mutate a federated credential except through updateCredential). For now the documentation fix in the docs finding covers it. Settle with a fixture provider that does not consume codes: a second login with the same code succeeds.

findings.claim: When the federated credential reports all codes used, the authenticator calls removeStoredCredentialById, which acts on local or fed storage only. The provider's copy is not removed, so only the added required action takes effect.
findings.evidence: mattpocock: :85-87 calls removeStoredCredentialById (local store only) when all codes are used. open-code-review: removeStoredCredentialById(federatedId) against local or fed storage does nothing to the provider's copy (:80-88). ponytail: for a federated credential that call cannot remove anything.
findings.reason: Accepted. On the federated branch, route removal through the provider (for example disableCredentialType) or skip the local removal call.

findings.claim: The fixture's getCredentials rebuilds the recovery-codes model with createFromValues, which drops the stored credential id. The returned model therefore has a null id, and delete or remove by id cannot find it.
findings.evidence: open-code-review: createFromValues does not copy the id generated at line 196, so account REST and CredentialDeleteHelper delete-by-id cannot find it. superpowers: CredentialDeleteHelper matches credentialId.equals(c.getId()) against the null id and throws NotFoundException. ponytail: the model is built without an id, so removeStoredCredentialById gets null.
findings.reason: Accepted. Set the stored id on the model returned from getCredentials.

coverage:
Files: all 8 patch files were reviewed by all four seats. open-code-review's tool left BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java out of its reviewable list (default_path), but the seat reviewed it manually. open-code-review and superpowers deliberately skipped the whitespace-only hunks (CredentialHelper re-indent, Javadoc

, test formatting). Not checked: the upstream GitHub issue (network blocked) and docs user-storage pages in depth (mattpocock); whether the new test passes and how imported-LDAP users behave at runtime (open-code-review); LDAP mappers and git history (superpowers). Axes that did not run: the gate was not run (benchmark mode), so the review is unanchored and no seat executed any build or test; every finding is reasoned, and no red test exists. There was no spec; mattpocock judged against the commit subject only. No reviewer from another model family took a seat. Merge only: no fixes were made, there were no rounds 2+, and no rejection verifiers were dispatched (none were needed, since no finding was rejected).
